exemplars.title: Learning Robust Models Using the Principle of Independent Causal Mechanisms
exemplars.why: Turns the ICM principle into a gradient-based invariance loss over environments; the learned stable relations generalize where ERM-trained models fail, which is the operational core of F5.
exemplars.quote: We propose a new gradient-based learning framework whose objective function is derived from the ICM principle.

exemplars.title: Can Large Language Models Learn Independent Causal Mechanisms?
exemplars.why: Implements ICM inside an LLM as multiple sparsely interacting language-modelling modules, and shows the modular/independence constraint improves OOD reasoning over a dense LLaMA2.
exemplars.quote: we apply two concepts from causality to learn ICMs within LLMs

exemplars.title: On the Generalization and Adaption Performance of Causal Models
exemplars.why: Systematically compares modular neural causal models (one mechanism per variable) against monolithic and non-causal structured models, finding an OOD/adaptation advantage that is strongest for sparse graphs.
exemplars.quote: the modular neural causal models outperform other models on both zero and few-shot adaptation in low data regimes and offer robust generalization

acl_llm_case.title: Robust agents learn causal world models
acl_llm_case.why: Agent-side counterpart: proves that regret-bounded agents facing many local distributional shifts must encode an approximate causal world model, linking F5 invariance to agent robustness.
acl_llm_case.quote: any agent capable of satisfying a regret bound for a large set of distributional shifts must have learned an approximate causal model of the data generating process

negative_case.title: CausalVerse: Benchmarking Causal Representation Learning with Configurable High-Fidelity Simulations
negative_case.why: Directly stress-tests the environment assumption: with corrupted domain labels the invariance method’s R² collapses from 0.29 to -6.77, so ICM-style learning is not robust when environments are mislabelled.
negative_case.quote: injecting incorrect domain labels is even more detrimental

evidence.when_not_to_use: Do not use when environments or intervention labels are unavailable, few, or corrupted, when mechanisms are known to interact, or when the target shift changes a mechanism that was never varied in training. Invariance penalties can then reduce to ERM or do worse.
evidence.notes: No CI_for_LLM paper learns ICM at LLM scale; 2402.02636 is coded OOD but is an LLM architecture paper. The acl_llm case 2402.10877 is theory/agent (tier C) and has no LLM experiment, so F5 still lacks an LLM-scale agent demonstration.

capabilities.name: Backdoor adjustment
capabilities.problem: Deconfounding observational ML; fairness; causal feature selection
capabilities.assumptions: No unmeasured confounders; positivity; correct graph
capabilities.failure_mode: Unmeasured confounding; bad adjustment sets; positivity violations

exemplars.title: Causal Policy Learning in Reinforcement Learning: Backdoor-Adjusted Soft Actor-Critic
exemplars.why: Implements the backdoor criterion as a policy operator: a learned Backdoor Reconstructor recovers pseudo-past variables so that pi(a|do(s)) can be estimated from confounded trajectories.
exemplars.quote: a principled extension of the SAC algorithm that corrects for hidden confounding via causal intervention estimation

exemplars.title: Scalable Causal Imitation Learning
exemplars.why: Scales sequential pi-backdoor adjustment to long-horizon imitation learning with a sliding-window adjustment set, giving an explicit deconfounded state representation.
exemplars.quote: causal imitation learning (CIL) provides a framework for approximating the expert’s policy from confounded data

exemplars.title: Technical Report: Facilitating the Adoption of Causal Inference Methods Through LLM-Empowered Co-Pilot
exemplars.why: Operationalizes backdoor identification as a tool: the LLM co-pilot builds an SCM and selects a minimal-uncertainty adjustment set before estimation.
exemplars.quote: identifying robust adjustment sets through a novel Minimal Uncertainty Adjustment Set criterion

acl_llm_case.title: Mitigating Hidden Confounding by Progressive Confounder Imputation via Large Language Models
acl_llm_case.why: LLM-based hidden-confounder imputation: ProCI generates and validates candidate confounders so standard backdoor/unconfoundedness estimators become applicable when no adjustment set is observed.
acl_llm_case.quote: We propose ProCI (Progressive Confounder Imputation), a framework that elicits the semantic and world knowledge of LLMs to iteratively generate, impute, and validate hidden confounders.

negative_case.title: The Confounder Trap: Treatment-Encoding Representations in Causal Inference with Text
negative_case.why: Shows the backdoor/overlap assumption can fail after representation learning: text representations encode the treatment and separate treated from control documents even when the causal problem itself has overlap.
negative_case.quote: richer representations can make treated and control documents separable, inducing overlap violations even when the underlying causal problem satisfies overlap

evidence.when_not_to_use: Do not use when confounders are unmeasured, the adjustment set is unknown or misspecified, or positivity fails. With text treatments, representations that encode treatment can silently destroy overlap; backdoor adjustment then returns a biased point estimate, not a bound.
evidence.notes: 2508.10581 is a co-pilot for adjustment-set selection rather than an estimator. 2607.26309 both diagnoses and fixes the failure; it is used as negative because it reports the assumption violation. No CI_for_LLM paper runs a classical backdoor ATE on LLM outputs with a validated graph.

exemplars.title: Causal Mean Field Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
exemplars.why: Models inter-agent interaction explicitly in an SCM and quantifies each interaction by intervention, instead of assuming agents are independent under mean-field factorization.

exemplars.title: Situation-Dependent Causal Influence-Based Cooperative Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning

exemplars.quote: Effective collaboration between agents thus requires a nuanced understanding of when and how agents’ actions influence others.

acl_llm_case.title: Hidden Messages Between Diffusion Language Model Agents: Causal Evidence for Latent Communication
acl_llm_case.why: Shows a compact hidden message from one diffusion-LM agent causally changes another agent’s answer (+63.6/+100 points), a concrete multi-agent interference channel that breaks no-interference.
acl_llm_case.quote: Removing a message tests whether the channel matters; replacing it with a message from another example tests whether its content matters.

negative_case.title: Do Latent Channels Actually Communicate? A Causal Audit of Latent Multi-Agent LLM Communication
negative_case.why: Audit finds the aggregate effect of a latent message mixes other-example content and reverses sign between 4B and 8B, so “the message” is not one consistent treatment version.
negative_case.quote: aggregate accuracy does not identify how a latent message affects the receiver

evidence.when_not_to_use: Do not use when treatment versions are ill-defined (prompt variants, regenerated messages) or when units interact through shared channels. A SUTVA-based ATE is not identified without an interference-aware design or cluster/network exposure mapping.
evidence.notes: No corpus paper explicitly tests SUTVA/consistency for prompt versions. The closest evidence is multi-agent LLM communication. 2607.26773 is an audit (tier C); its negative result is treatment-version ambiguity rather than a formal SUTVA test.

exemplars.title: Text-Transport: Toward Learning Causal Effects of Natural Language
exemplars.why: Text-Transport derives a density-ratio transport estimator with statistical guarantees for moving a text causal effect from a source distribution to any target distribution.
exemplars.quote: we leverage the notion of distribution shift to describe an estimator that transports causal effects between domains

exemplars.title: When Distributions Shifts: Causal Generalization for Low-Resource Languages
exemplars.why: Applies causal DG/CRL across low-resource language distributions and reports OOD gains, i.e. a causal model trained on some languages is carried to unseen ones.
exemplars.quote: enhanced out-of-distribution performance from causal representation learning across multiple languages

acl_llm_case.title: Do LLMs Have the Generalization Ability in Conducting Causal Inference?
acl_llm_case.why: Tests whether LLMs can carry causal inference (including backdoor adjustment) to unseen phenomena and new variable names, the LLM analogue of transporting a causal estimator to a target domain.
acl_llm_case.quote: We extensively tested the generalization capabilities of five leading LLMs across four tasks

negative_case.title: Collaborative Heterogeneous Causal Inference Beyond Meta-analysis
negative_case.why: States the central transport failure: source-site re-weighting/meta-analysis breaks when a site does not cover the target population, i.e. target support is missing.
negative_case.quote: this method could easily fail when a certain site couldn’t cover the entire population

evidence.when_not_to_use: Do not use when no target-domain data or selection diagram is available, or when the target lies outside the support of every source site. The transport formula then rests on untestable selection assumptions and can be worse than a local estimate.
evidence.notes: No CI_for_LLM paper applies a formal selection-diagram transport formula. 2410.11385 is the closest LLM transport test but evaluates task generalization, not a transport estimand. 2404.15746 is tier C; its negative evidence is a stated failure of prior re-weighting, not a head-to-head experiment.

exemplars.title: Reinforcement Learning of Causal Variables Using Mediation Analysis
exemplars.why: Uses the natural indirect effect as the RL objective, so the learned causal variable is defined by a mediation target rather than expected return.
exemplars.quote: causal variables and policies are determined by maximizing a new optimization target inspired by mediation analysis

exemplars.title: Pessimistic Causal Reinforcement Learning with Mediators for Confounded Offline Data
exemplars.why: Uses mediator-based front-door adjustment to handle unmeasured confounding in offline RL, making the mediator distribution the object that is pessimistically bounded.
exemplars.quote: We utilize the mediator variable based on front-door criterion to remove the confounding bias

acl_llm_case.title: Identifying and Adapting Transformer-Components Responsible for Gender Bias in an English Language Model
acl_llm_case.why: Applies causal mediation analysis to GPT-2 to localize components responsible for gender bias, then fine-tunes exactly those components — mediation as an intervention target in an LLM.
acl_llm_case.quote: we study three methods for identifying causal relations between LM components and particular output: causal mediation analysis, automated circuit discovery and our novel, efficient method called DiffMask+

negative_case.title: Ice Cream Doesn't Cause Drowning: Benchmarking LLMs Against Statistical Pitfalls in Causal Inference
negative_case.why: Benchmark reports that LLMs ignore mediator–outcome confounding and attribute the whole effect to the mediator, the core identification failure for NDE/NIE.
negative_case.quote: LLMs frequently overlook this bias: they may attribute the entire treatment effect to the mediating variable or misestimate indirect and direct effects because they ignore hidden pathways.

evidence.when_not_to_use: Do not use when mediator–outcome confounding or cross-world independence is untenable, or when treatment–mediator interaction is the object. NDE/NIE are then not identified, and natural effects can be misleading even when total effects are valid.
evidence.notes: No corpus paper estimates NDE/NIE on LLM text with mediator–outcome confounding made explicit. 2310.12611 does component-level mediation; 2505.13770 reports the failure but is a benchmark (tier C).

capabilities.name: Partial identification

capabilities.failure_mode: Bounds too wide; assumptions still matter

exemplars.title: A Neural Framework for Generalized Causal Sensitivity Analysis
exemplars.why: Implements generalized causal sensitivity analysis with two conditional normalizing flows, producing valid bounds under MSM, f-sensitivity and Rosenbaum models for ATE and CATE, so sensitivity analysis is the method rather than a caveat.
exemplars.quote: Unlike previous work, our framework is compatible with (i) a large class of sensitivity models

exemplars.title: Sharp Bounds for Generalized Causal Sensitivity Analysis
exemplars.why: Derives sharp bounds for a generalized marginal sensitivity model and a scalable estimator, turning sensitivity analysis into explicit partial identification under unobserved confounding.
exemplars.quote: we propose a flexible generalization of the marginal sensitivity model (MSM) and then derive sharp bounds for a large class of causal effects

exemplars.title: Two-way Deconfounder for Off-policy Evaluation in Causal Reinforcement Learning
exemplars.why: Runs an explicit sensitivity analysis with parameter Γ that increasingly violates its own two-way unconfoundedness assumption, so the robustness of the off-policy estimate is measured instead of asserted.
exemplars.quote: we investigate how TWD performs when the proposed TWUC assumption is violated

acl_llm_case.title: Using large language models for sensitivity analysis in causal inference: case studies on Cornfield inequality and E-value
acl_llm_case.why: Four LLMs are prompted to compute E-values and Cornfield inequalities and to interpret robustness; ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini reproduce the E-values while DeepSeek shows small biases, making it the LLM case for sensitivity analysis.
acl_llm_case.quote: We assess four widely used LLMs, ChatGPT, Claude, DeepSeek, and Gemini, on their ability to conduct sensitivity analyses using Cornfield inequalities and E-values

negative_case.title: Causality-driven Hierarchical Structure Discovery for Reinforcement Learning
negative_case.why: The paper labels an environment-variable completeness check a 'sensitivity analysis', but it perturbs EV quality, not an unmeasured-confounder parameter, so the capability is named without being implemented.
negative_case.quote: We conduct sensitivity analysis experiments of EV in appendix A that verify the quality of EV does not seriously hurt the performance of CDHRL

evidence.when_not_to_use: Do not use when the sensitivity parameter has no domain interpretation or when the resulting bounds are too wide to change a decision. Sensitivity analysis does not identify the effect, does not repair a bad adjustment set, and must not be reported as a significance test.
evidence.notes: 2311.16026 and 2305.16988 are C-tier because every comparator is another causal sensitivity method; 2412.05783 is the only B-tier exemplar. No A-tier paper in this corpus implements E-value/Rosenbaum bounds as its main method for AI systems. 2210.06964 is A-tier but its 'sensitivity analysis' is an EV-quality ablation, so it is used only as negative evidence.

exemplars.title: Causal Evaluation of Membership Inference Attacks

exemplars.quote: Proposition 4.1 naturally suggests an inverse probability weighting (IPW) estimator

exemplars.title: A Technical Exploration of Causal Inference with Hybrid LLM Synthetic Data
exemplars.why: Builds propensity and outcome models on LLM-generated data and adds a synthetic pairing step explicitly aimed at positivity violations, benchmarking IPTW, AIPW and substitution estimators.
exemplars.quote: We further introduce a synthetic pairing strategy to mitigate positivity violations

exemplars.title: Collaborative Heterogeneous Causal Inference Beyond Meta-analysis
exemplars.why: Proposes a collaborative inverse-propensity-score-weighting estimator across heterogeneous sites, making propensity reweighting the core estimator rather than a preprocessing step.
exemplars.quote: we propose a collaborative inverse propensity score weighting estimator for causal inference with heterogeneous data

acl_llm_case.title: The Confounder Trap: Treatment-Encoding Representations in Causal Inference with Text
acl_llm_case.why: Shows that when treatment status is encoded in text, learned representations make treated and control documents separable, so propensity scores degenerate and overlap fails even though the causal problem has overlap.
acl_llm_case.quote: richer representations can make treated and control documents separable, inducing overlap violations even when the underlying causal problem satisfies overlap

negative_case.title: Estimating Causal Effects of Text Interventions Leveraging LLMs
negative_case.why: In its text-intervention benchmark the IPW baseline is significantly worse than the proposed DANN estimator, which the authors read as a failure of propensity-score estimation.
negative_case.quote: the results show that IPW has significantly worse performance, suggesting issues with propensity score estimation

evidence.when_not_to_use: Do not use when overlap fails or treated and control units are separable (text and embedding treatments make this likely), when unmeasured confounding is plausible because propensity scores balance only observed covariates, or when matching would discard most of a small sample.
evidence.notes: 2607.26309 is the strongest positivity evidence but is used as the ACL/LLM case. 2404.15746 is C and purely statistical; 2602.02819 is L1 because its causal machinery is post-processing of scores. If a second B-tier text-treatment exemplar is needed, 2410.21474 covers it but its IPW arm fails, so it is used as the negative.

capabilities.name: IP weighting / MSM
capabilities.assumptions: No unmeasured confounding; positivity; correct weights

capabilities.name: Doubly robust / AIPW / TMLE
capabilities.assumptions: One of treatment/outcome models correct; positivity
capabilities.exemplars: Bang & Robins 2005; van der Laan & Rubin 2006

exemplars.title: CaMeWM: A Causal Medical World Model for Generative Tumor Evolution and Treatment Planning
exemplars.why: Uses a support-restricted, factual-only cross-fitted AIPW-RMST estimate as the primary policy evaluation, so AIPW is the reported estimator rather than an add-on.
exemplars.quote: The primary policy estimate is factual-only cross-fitted AIPW-RMST

exemplars.title: Deep learning based doubly robust test for Granger causality
exemplars.why: Builds a doubly robust Granger test whose statistic combines neural nuisance estimators with a multiplier bootstrap, applying the DR principle to hypothesis testing.
exemplars.quote: we propose a doubly robust Granger causality test (DRGCT)

exemplars.title: InferenceEvolve: Towards Automated Causal Effect Estimators through Self-Evolving AI
exemplars.why: Constructs cross-fitted doubly robust pseudo-outcomes and AIPW estimates as the proxy evaluation signal for automatically generated estimators.
exemplars.quote: We construct cross-fitted doubly-robust pseudo-outcomes following Kennedy (2024)

acl_llm_case.title: Optimizing Language Models for Human Preferences is a Causal Inference Problem
acl_llm_case.why: Extends causal preference optimization to DR-CPO, adding a doubly robust correction to an LLM preference-learning objective with stated bias guarantees.
acl_llm_case.quote: We further extend CPO with doubly robust CPO (DR-CPO), which reduces the variance of the surrogate objective while retaining provably strong guarantees on bias

negative_case.title: Stochastic intervention for causal inference via reinforcement learning
negative_case.why: Reports that TMLE is competitive in training but degrades out of sample and has very large test variance, an explicit finite-sample failure of the DR/TMLE family.
negative_case.quote: although TMLE performs well in the training set, its performance likely degrades when dealing with out-of-sample data in the testing set

evidence.when_not_to_use: Do not use with small N and many nuisance functions, near-positivity violations where both models are wrong, or when AIPW/TMLE variance dominates the bias gain. Doubly robust consistency is asymptotic and does not rescue a failed overlap assumption.
evidence.notes: Only 2610.26923 is B; 2509.15798 and 2604.04274 are C, and the negative 2105.13514 is C. The corpus contains no A-tier TMLE paper; AIPW mostly appears as a component or baseline, so the exemplar set over-represents applied uses over estimator theory.

capabilities.name: Double machine learning
capabilities.failure_mode: Weak overlap; many nuisances; small N

exemplars.title: Causal Inference with Generative Artificial Intelligence: Application to Texts as Treatments
exemplars.why: Applies double machine learning with cross-fitting to estimate ATEs of text treatments from LLM representations, and itself reports DML+BERT failing under strong confounding, so DML is used and stress-tested.
exemplars.quote: derive the asymptotic properties of the proposed estimator through the application of double machine learning

exemplars.title: CausalMix: Data Mixture as Causal Inference for Language Model Training
exemplars.why: Fits CausalForestDML on 512 training runs and extrapolates CATE-optimal data mixtures to a 7B model, so DML drives the decision rather than illustrating it.
exemplars.quote: CausalForestDML achieves the best performance

acl_llm_case.title: Optimizing Prompts for Large Language Models: A Causal Approach
acl_llm_case.why: Learns a DML causal reward model over prompt and query embeddings and uses its output to search prompts, making DML the core of an LLM method.
acl_llm_case.quote: it learns an offline causal reward model by applying Double Machine Learning (DML) to semantic embeddings of prompts and queries

negative_case.title: Leveraging Generative Artificial Intelligence for Causal Inference with Unstructured Data
negative_case.why: Its AIPW–DML baseline has severe bias and 0.56 coverage under a positivity violation, a concrete collapse of the DML estimator when overlap fails.
negative_case.quote: the two baselines, DragonNet and AIPW–DML, suffer from severe bias

evidence.when_not_to_use: Do not use when overlap is weak, when N is small relative to the number of nuisances or cross-fitting folds, or when nuisance models are unstable. DML removes first-order regularization bias but not confounding or positivity violations.
evidence.notes: Only two exemplars: the corpus has no A-tier DML-only method paper, and 2507.03897 (the clearest DML failure) is used as the negative. 2410.00903 also reports DML+BERT performing poorly under strong confounding, so the exemplar is not an unqualified success story.

capabilities.name: Heterogeneous effects
capabilities.assumptions: Unconfoundedness; overlap; enough data per stratum
capabilities.exemplars: Athey et al. 2019; Künzel et al. 2019

exemplars.title: From Text to Treatment Effects: A Meta-Learning Approach to Handling Text-Based Confounding
exemplars.why: Benchmarks T-, RA-, DR- and R-learners for CATE when confounders are expressed as text, and shows text embeddings beat no-confounder baselines while still falling short of true confounders.
exemplars.quote: Meta-learners leveraging text embeddings of confounders—whether from domain-specific or general-purpose encoders—outperform those without access to confounders

exemplars.title: Training and Evaluating Causal Forecasting Models for Time-Series
exemplars.why: Trains causal time-series models with an orthogonal R-loss to estimate CATEs and validates them against RDD estimates built from the same series.
exemplars.quote: to train causal time-series models that generalize better when forecasting the effect of actions outside of their training distribution

exemplars.title: Meta-Router: Bridging Gold-standard and Preference-based Evaluations in Large Language Model Routing
exemplars.why: Estimates CATE with R- and DR-learners to remove preference-data bias in LLM routing, so heterogeneous-effect estimation is the core of the method.
exemplars.quote: meta-router training framework that corrects preference-data bias through R- and DR-learners for CATE estimation

acl_llm_case.title: Mitigating Hidden Confounding by Progressive Confounder Imputation via Large Language Models
acl_llm_case.why: Uses LLM-imputed hidden confounders to improve CATE estimators and reports that vanilla CFR-Wass and ESCFR degrade as confounders are removed, making it the LLM case for heterogeneous effects.
acl_llm_case.quote: the performance of vanilla CATE estimators CFR-Wass and ESCFR degrades significantly across all metrics

negative_case.title: A Distributionally Robust Framework for Nuisance in Causal Effect Estimation
negative_case.why: Shows that with only noisy CATE labels the MSE does not converge to zero even as N grows, so absolute CATE accuracy is not identified and only relative comparisons are meaningful.
negative_case.quote: even as the sample size N approaches infinity, the MSE for this noisy CATE estimate does not converge to zero

evidence.when_not_to_use: Do not use when subgroups are sparse, when unconfoundedness is doubtful (CATE inherits the confounding bias of the average effect), or when the decision needs a population-level effect. CATE estimates are unstable under weak overlap and usually lack individual ground truth.
evidence.notes: 2409.15503 is B because all arms are CATE estimators; 2411.00126 and 2509.25535 are A. The negative 2505.17717 is C and its statement concerns noisy evaluation labels rather than a failed estimator, so it is a partial negative (evaluation floor rather than estimation failure).

capabilities.name: Constraint-based discovery (PC/FCI)
capabilities.assumptions: Markov; faithfulness; causal sufficiency (PC) or latent confounders (FCI)
capabilities.exemplars: Spirtes et al. 1991; Spirtes et al. 2001

exemplars.title: Large Language Models for Constrained-Based Causal Discovery
exemplars.why: Implements chatPC by substituting an LLM conditional-independence oracle into an existing PC implementation, so constraint-based skeleton search and orientation are actually run.
exemplars.quote: we plug in the LLM-based conditional independence testing to an existing PC implementation

exemplars.title: Leveraging Large Language Models for Causal Discovery: a Constraint-based, Argumentation-driven Approach
exemplars.why: Runs an MPC skeleton and Causal ABA over CI facts plus LLM-derived arrow constraints, giving a concrete constraint-based DAG search.
exemplars.quote: ABAPC-LLM combines CI evidence from data with semantic arrow constraints elicited from LLMs

exemplars.title: CauTion: Knowing When to Trust LLMs for Ensemble Causal Discovery
exemplars.why: Uses PC as one of the algorithm-ensemble members and documents the exact ensemble, so constraint-based discovery is operationalized rather than merely cited.
exemplars.quote: We use PC, GES and CAMML as the algorithm ensemble for all experiments

acl_llm_case.title: Integrating Large Language Models in Causal Discovery: A Statistical Causal Approach
acl_llm_case.why: Adds LLM-derived edge constraints to the PC algorithm (among other structure-discovery methods) and evaluates the augmented graphs, making it the LLM case for constraint-based discovery.
acl_llm_case.quote: the Peter- Clark (PC) algorithm ( Spirtes et al., 2000 ) is augmented with background knowledge of the forced or forbidden directed edges
acl_llm_case.locator: §2 Related Work and Originality in Our Work

negative_case.title: Consistency evaluation of benchmarks used for causal discovery
negative_case.why: Checks 11 popular benchmark graphs against domain literature and finds their ground truth varies in consistency, so D1's evaluation premise of a reliable ground-truth DAG is itself unstable.
negative_case.quote: popular benchmarks vary significantly in their consistency with domain research, with clear implications for causal discovery research

evidence.when_not_to_use: Do not use when faithfulness or causal sufficiency is doubtful, when CI tests are underpowered, or when the graph is large enough that PC/FCI's repeated CI queries are infeasible; an LLM CI oracle is not a substitute for calibrated tests.
evidence.notes: Only 2406.07378 is B, and it is L1; 2602.16481 and 2606.03602 are C/L2. No A-tier pure PC/FCI method paper exists in this corpus. 2606.03602 uses PC, GES and CAMML (not FCI), so it is an ensemble case rather than a pure constraint-based method. 2606.01789 is a benchmark-audit paper with an explicit negative conclusion, not a generic review.

exemplars.title: Regularized Multi-LLMs Collaboration for Enhanced Score-based Causal Discovery
exemplars.why: Adds a multi-LLM penalty term to the GES and NOTEARS scoring objectives, directly instantiating score-based discovery.
exemplars.quote: we incorporate the findings from LLMs into our causal discovery scoring function by introducing an additional penalty

exemplars.title: Reinforcement Learning for Causal Discovery without Acyclicity Constraints
exemplars.why: Trains an RL policy over Vec2DAG, a surjective unconstrained DAG parameterization, for score-based discovery without an explicit acyclicity constraint.
exemplars.quote: Recently, reinforcement learning (RL) has proved a promising alternative for conventional local heuristics in score-based approaches to learning directed acyclic causal graphs

exemplars.title: LLM-initialized Differentiable Causal Discovery
exemplars.why: Initializes a differentiable maximum-likelihood DAG objective with an LLM adjacency matrix, implementing a NOTEARS-style continuous score search.
exemplars.quote: LLM-DCD, which uses an LLM to initialize the optimization of the maximum likelihood objective function of DCD approaches

acl_llm_case.title: Causal Structure Learning Supervised by Large Language Model
acl_llm_case.why: Uses GPT-4 to produce structural priors that enter a score-based structure-learning objective, giving an LLM-supervised score-based case.
acl_llm_case.quote: the score-based method is chosen as the backbone CSL algorithm in our ILS-CSL framework

negative_case.title: Effects of Distributional Biases on Gradient-Based Causal Discovery in the Bivariate Categorical Case
negative_case.why: Shows gradient-based causal discovery is biased by marginal distribution asymmetries even in controlled bivariate categorical data, undercutting the score/differentiable assumptions behind D2.
negative_case.quote: Those approaches however can be susceptible to distributional biases in the data they are trained on.

evidence.when_not_to_use: Do not use when the score is misspecified, when the graph is large or high-dimensional, or when acyclicity is only softly enforced; local optima, scaling and distributional biases can make the recovered graph or orientation unreliable.
evidence.notes: All three exemplars are C because every comparator in these papers is another causal-discovery method; this corpus contains no A/B pure score-based method paper. 2509.01621 studies bivariate gradient-based discovery rather than full NOTEARS, but directly tests the differentiable-score assumption.

capabilities.name: Functional causal models (LiNGAM/ANM)
capabilities.assumptions: Linear non-Gaussian or additive noise; acyclicity
capabilities.exemplars: Shimizu et al. 2006; Hoyer et al. 2008

exemplars.title: Why LLMs Fail at Causal Discovery and How Interventional Agents Escape
exemplars.why: Uses a frozen LLM as an interventional oracle inside a Bayesian loop that selects targeted intervention queries, implementing active interventional discovery.
exemplars.quote: a frozen language model serves as an interventional oracle answering targeted queries about intervention effects, while an external Bayesian loop concentrates beliefs over candidate graphs

exemplars.title: Amortized Active Causal Induction with Deep Reinforcement Learning
exemplars.why: Learns an amortized RL policy that selects do()-interventions to maximize a causal-graph posterior, directly implementing interventional design.
exemplars.quote: an active intervention design policy that can select interventions that are adaptive, real-time and that does not require access to the likelihood

exemplars.title: Causal Curiosity: RL Agents Discovering Self-supervised Experiments for Causal Representation Learning
exemplars.why: Trains RL agents with a causal curiosity reward to choose experiments that identify causal factors, implementing active intervention selection.
exemplars.quote: we attempt to equip reinforcement learning agents with the ability to perform experiments that facilitate a categorization of the rolled-out trajectories

exemplars.title: Can Large Language Models Help Experimental Design for Causal Discovery?
exemplars.why: LeGIT uses an LLM to propose intervention targets inside an online causal-discovery loop, instantiating LLM-guided experimental design.
exemplars.quote: a robust framework that effectively incorporates LLMs to augment existing numerical approaches for the intervention targeting in causal discovery

acl_llm_case.title: Passive learning of active causal strategies in agents and language models
acl_llm_case.why: Shows passive agents and a 70B Chinchilla LM can learn to intervene at test time and infer causal structure, making it the LLM/agent case for active causal strategies.
acl_llm_case.quote: purely passive learning can in fact allow an agent to learn generalizable strategies for determining and using causal structures, as long as the agent can intervene at test time

negative_case.title: Parameter Estimation using Reinforcement Learning Causal Curiosity: Limits and Challenges
negative_case.why: Re-analyses Causal Curiosity and reports that multiple simultaneously varying parameters are unsolvable in the studied complex settings, exposing a limit of active interventional discovery.
negative_case.quote: we show the impossibility of solving some complex experimental situations studied for the first time here with multiple parameters varying simultaneously

evidence.when_not_to_use: Do not use when interventions are expensive or restricted to few targets, when the intervention target is unknown, or when faithfulness and budget assumptions fail; active selection can be worse than passive data collection.
evidence.notes: 2503.01139 is C/L4 but included as a fourth exemplar of LLM-guided experimental design. 2605.27567's A tier depends on a same-model ablation with an unmatched inference budget, per the corpus coding notes.

capabilities.name: Time-series discovery
capabilities.failure_mode: Granger is predictive, not causal; nonstationarity

exemplars.title: MotifDisco: Motif Causal Discovery For Time Series Motifs
exemplars.why: Defines motif causality and learns a directed causal graph among motifs with a GNN link-prediction objective, implementing time-series causal discovery.
exemplars.quote: we develop a causal discovery framework to learn MC amongst a set of ordered motifs pulled from time series traces

exemplars.title: Embracing the black box: Heading towards foundation models for causal discovery from time series data
exemplars.why: Trains a supervised end-to-end map from multivariate time series to causal graphs and tests scaling, implementing amortized time-series discovery.
exemplars.quote: A methodology that aims to learn a direct mapping from multivariate time series to the underlying causal graphs in a supervised manner.

exemplars.title: Explainable Online Unsupervised Anomaly Detection for Cyber-Physical Systems via Causal Discovery from Time Series
exemplars.why: Runs PCMCI on normal sensor time series and monitors link persistence for online anomaly detection, a direct PCMCI-based time-series discovery pipeline.
exemplars.quote: we use state-of-the-art PCMCI algorithm [ 15 ] to learn normal causal links

acl_llm_case.title: Augur: Modeling Covariate Causal Associations in Time Series via Large Language Models
acl_llm_case.why: Augur uses a teacher LLM plus pairwise causality testing to infer a directed covariate graph for forecasting, giving the LLM/time-series case.
acl_llm_case.quote: Augur uses a two stage teacher student architecture where a powerful teacher LLM infers a directed causal graph from time series using heuristic search together with pairwise causality testing.

negative_case.title: CausalCompass: Evaluating the Robustness of Time-Series Causal Discovery in Misspecified Scenarios
negative_case.why: Benchmarks TSCD methods under eight assumption violations and finds no method consistently optimal, directly challenging D5's stationarity and lag-order assumptions.
negative_case.quote: no single method consistently attains optimal performance across all settings

evidence.when_not_to_use: Do not use when the series is nonstationary, when the lag order is unknown or misspecified, or when the target is an interventional effect rather than prediction; Granger/PCMCI recover predictive lag structure, not necessarily causal effects.
evidence.notes: 2602.07915 is a D-tier benchmark used only as negative evidence; it is not a pure review and reports explicit robustness failures. The corpus has applied PCMCI pipelines but no A/B method paper dedicated to PCMCI itself.

capabilities.name: Identifiable causal representation
capabilities.exemplars: Yang et al. 2021; Khemakhem et al. 2020

exemplars.title: Causal Representation Learning for Instantaneous and Temporal Effects in Interactive Systems
exemplars.why: Proves identifiability of minimal causal variables with instantaneous effects and jointly learns the causal graph via differentiable discovery.
exemplars.quote: iCITRIS identifies the potentially multidimensional causal variables from temporal observations, while simultaneously using a differentiable causal discovery method to learn their causal graph

exemplars.title: Identifiable Causal Representation Learning: Unsupervised, Multi-View, and Multi-Environment
exemplars.why: Develops IMA and multi-environment identifiability results and validates IMA-regularized learning, directly addressing identifiable causal representation learning.
exemplars.quote: for a multi-environment setting of learning from non-identically distributed datasets arising from perfect single-node interventions, we show that the latents and their causal graph are identifiable

exemplars.title: Towards Unsupervised Causal Representation Learning via Latent Additive Noise Model Causal Autoencoders
exemplars.why: Operationalizes an additive noise model as a structural layer in a causal autoencoder, with identifiability analysis for unsupervised causal representation learning.
exemplars.quote: we propose the Latent Additive Noise Model Causal Autoencoder (LANCA) to operationalize the Additive Noise Model (ANM) as a strong inductive bias for unsupervised discovery

acl_llm_case.title: Language Agents Meet Causality -- Bridging LLMs and Causal World Models
acl_llm_case.why: Couples CRL-learned causal variables to natural-language expressions so an LLM agent can query a causal world model, giving the LLM case for identifiable representations.
acl_llm_case.quote: We propose a framework that integrates CRLs with LLMs to enable causally-aware reasoning and planning.

negative_case.title: Sanity Checking Causal Representation Learning on a Simple Real-World System
negative_case.why: Tests representative CRL methods on a real optical system with known factors and finds they all fail to recover them consistently, showing D6's identifiability guarantees do not transfer to practice.
negative_case.quote: We select methods representative of different approaches to CRL and find that they all fail to consistently recover the underlying causal factors.

evidence.when_not_to_use: Do not use when the mixing function is arbitrary nonlinear, when auxiliary variables or interventions are unavailable, or when evaluation lacks ground-truth factors; identifiability theorems do not guarantee finite-sample recovery.
evidence.notes: 2410.19923 is the closest CI_for_LLM case; it uses BISCUIT-style CRL but is not itself a new identifiability method. 2502.20099 is a C-tier benchmark used as an empirical negative; 2312.03580 is an alternative theory-only negative with impossibility results.
